image.altText: Two men in wetsuits stand together near water

children.content: The parents of Callum and Jake Robinson come face to face with their sons' alleged killers at the start of a murder trial in Mexico, with the accused men later removed from the courtroom after prosecutors said witnesses had been intimidated.

items.title: Australian navy saves Canadian sailor from sinking catamaran in Indian Ocean

children.content: Australian authorities executed the textbook helicopter rescue after the Canadian sailor's vessel began taking on water 1,000 kilometres south-east of Christmas Island.

children.content: A 70-year-old man has died after being run over by a garbage truck in Perth's south-eastern suburbs, with neighbours remembering as a quiet, sweet person.

items.title: ASX down, building company collapse exposes private credit issues

children.content: The Australian share market has fallen as oil prices jump to seven-week high after flare-up in US-Iran tensions. The Bathla Group collapse exposes private credit issues and oil is up on Middle East tensions. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Bathla suspensions point to 'larger storm' coming in construction industry

children.content: Under voluntary administration and having stood down two-thirds its staff, embattled property developer Bathla Group leaves dozens of projects in limbo.

image.altText: a house nearly complete surrounded by scaffold fencing

items.title: Aussie startup cuts staff, pivots to US after $32m government outlay

children.content: Harrison.ai is laying off staff and pivoting to a new US business model, a year after receiving a $32 million investment from the federal government to keep the company in Australia.

items.title: Elder among last to remember Australia's forgotten 'parkland'

children.content: Menang elder Aunty Carol Petterson remembers when her family worked as shepherds, driving sheep through the bushland and along rivers towards the coast in southern Western Australia. Decades later, she recalls in vivid detail the natural abundance of the landscape.

children.content: The spread of avian flu to a fox in metropolitan Adelaide has experts calling for city dwellers, not just farmers, to be part of the solution in tackling the pests.

items.title: Day sailings to end with new Spirit of Tasmania ferries

children.content: The Spirit of Tasmania ferry service between Tasmania and the mainland will take no paying passengers for a week in late October as new ships are tested.

items.title: Ex-Eagle says 'conservative and vanilla' AFL club's main focus is money

children.content: Former West Coast Eagles player Sharrod Wellingham says the club has become complacent because of its financial might and needs to refocus on winning games.

items.title: Autonomous drones and AI called out by UN human rights chief

children.content: The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights has addressed a council in Geneva saying AI posed a threat to humanity among the use of autonomous drones and US deaths in immigration custody.

items.title: 50 years of spotting southern right whales off Great Australian Bight

children.content: From WA's capital to SA's far west coast, scientists have collated 50 years' worth of data on the southern right whale to track changes to breeding cycles.

items.title: Perth looks back to the day when Mundaring Weir last overflowed

children.content: Thirty years ago, Perth's Mundaring Weir overflowed following good winter rains. The visitors who flocked to see the spectacle had no idea it would never happen again.

items.title: Mixed emotions as Andreeva embraces injured idol after US Open win

children.content: Mirra Andreeva says it was hard to be purely happy after beating an injured Anastasia Potapova in the fourth round of the US Open after the Russian-born Austrian's late knee injury.

image.altText: Mirra Andreeva bends over to check on an injured Anatasia Potapova at the US Open.
